---
title: "Introduction"
---

## Scope Defined

For this project, we are focusing on **Data Scientists in the Scientific Research and Development Services industry (NAICS 5417)**.

We want to better understand what the job market looks like for Data Scientists in this industry, especially the skills employers are looking for. We will also look at factors such as salary, location, experience requirements, work arrangements, and the companies hiring for these positions.

Using the MET Career Compass 2026 dataset, we narrowed the data to Data Scientist job postings within NAICS 5417. After cleaning and preparing the data, our final dataset contains **760 job postings** that will be used throughout the project.

## Target User

Our target users are **students and early-career job seekers who are interested in becoming Data Scientists or pursuing similar data-focused careers**.

It can be difficult to know which skills to focus on when preparing for a career in data science. Job postings often list a wide range of programming languages, software tools, technical skills, and experience requirements. Our goal is to make that information easier to understand by identifying the skills that appear most often in actual job postings.

This can help someone compare their current skills with what employers are looking for and decide which areas they may want to strengthen as they prepare for the job market.

## Product Question

**What skills are most in demand for Data Scientists within Scientific Research and Development Services (NAICS 5417)?**

## Rationale

We chose to focus on skills because knowing that Data Scientist jobs are available is only part of understanding the career market. Someone preparing for these roles also needs to know **what employers expect applicants to know**.

Data Scientist positions can require a mix of programming, data analysis, statistics, machine learning, and other technical skills. The exact combination can also vary depending on the industry and the type of work being done.

By focusing on **Scientific Research and Development Services (NAICS 5417)**, we can look at these requirements within a specific industry rather than combining Data Scientist jobs from many different industries.

Our analysis will identify the skills and software tools that appear most frequently in these job postings. Later in the project, we can use these results as a benchmark for the Skill Gap Analysis and Career Evaluation.


## Literature Review

### Industry Spotlight - Scientific Research and Development Services Industry Profile

This report gives an outline of employment prospectives for individuals in Scientific Research and Development Services roles. The report gives employment statistics, wage statistics, regional variations, and growth potential.
It shows wage growth increasing while overall employments slows down, it shows the sector with the highest employment being "Management, Scientific, and Technical Consulting Services" and the sector with the highest wages being 
"Scientific Research and Development Services." [@chmura2023industry]

### Bridging digital skill gaps in the global workforce: A synthesis and conceptual framework building

This article discusses skill gaps in the global workforce with an emphasis on the lack of digital capabilities. The article shows the measurable gaps in digital skills such as digital tools and applications, and data analysis with the 
available workforce that is hampering productivity in the global economy. The paper recommends national digital skilling initiatives that are inclusive to all demographics. [@mhaske2025skills]

### Researcher of the Future: 6 skills for a scientific career

This article breaks down the skills needed for the future of research roles. The top skills emphasized by the author are strategic thinking, interdisciplinary functionality, data and AI, project management, and continuous learning. From this article the 
emphasis and data and AI for researchers in the future is a mandatory requirement that anyone looking to get into R&D will need if they wish to be successful in these fields. [@ribas2026researcher]
